title: the Fens Rising Again
premise: August Whitlock, archivist of Ely Cathedral, receives two letters about a thirty-year-old drowning in the Fens: one confessing to the crime, the other promising a second death. When the confessed killer is found dead in the locked crypt before police can act, August realizes the letters were bait — someone is using her archive to stage a perfect murder and frame a dead man. Following the paper trail through parish records, she discovers the victim's identity was swapped decades ago, and that the killer is the investigator who closed the original case, now protecting his own buried past. In the flooded crypt at spring tide, August traps him with the forged document he needed her to authenticate, choosing truth over the loyalty of an old friend who helped cover the first crime.
about_author: Coral Reyes spent a decade cataloguing ecclesiastical archives in East Anglia before turning to fiction full-time. She writes mysteries where documents remember what people would rather forget.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: August Whitlock sorts a bequest of papers when twin letters arrive: one confessing to the 1994 drowning of a fenland girl, one promising 'the second will follow.' Both are written in the same hand as a genuine 1994 case file she once catalogued. POV: August. Beat: unease — the past has found her address.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Wasn't Missed
chapters.summary: August pulls the original file from restricted storage and finds the victim listed under a name that belongs to a woman still alive in Norfolk. The drowned girl was someone else entirely — erased by a clerical swap no one questioned. POV: August, with a flashback fragment of the real girl. Beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Inspector Holloway's Cold Case
chapters.summary: Retired DI Edmund Holloway, who closed the 1994 case, visits the cathedral asking casually after the letters. Charming, precise, he quotes details only the killer or the lead investigator could know. August lies to him for the first time in her life. POV: alternating August and Holloway. Beat: cat-and-mouse begins; Holloway knows she knows.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: August finds the crypt lock freshly scratched and a ledger page razored out — records of a 1994 burial moved without authorization. Her oldest friend, verger Tom Beddoe, urges her to hand everything to police and stop digging. POV: August. Beat: loyalty strains against truth; Tom is hiding something too.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Arrives
chapters.summary: A second promise arrives naming its victim: Tom. August begs him to leave town; he refuses, confessing he drove the getaway car in 1994 for a man he loved like a brother. That night the crypt floods early with the spring tide. POV: August, then Tom's final hours. Beat: guilt, tenderness, impending loss.

chapters.title: Drowned Twice
chapters.summary: Tom is found in the flooded crypt — drowned in inches of water, drugged first, staged to mirror the 1994 scene exactly. Police read it as suicide-by-guilt. August alone sees the choreography: the killer is reenacting the file, page by page. POV: August amid grief. Beat: rage hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: The Forger's Signature
chapters.summary: Comparing handwriting across decades, August proves the confession letter was written recently on period paper — and that the same hand altered the 1994 name register. Only one person had access to both: the investigating officer who 'closed' the case. POV: August, racing the tide calendar. Beat: the trap designs itself.

chapters.title: Authentication
chapters.summary: August lets word slip that she's authenticated a document proving Holloway's real identity — the name he buried in 1994. She plants it in the crypt archive, knowing he must destroy it himself before the diocesan audit. POV: Holloway, finally inside his head. Beat: cold satisfaction shading into fear as he takes the bait.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Holloway comes for the document at high water; August locks them both in, recording his confession as the water rises and he recounts the original killing — a girl who learned his name. Police, tipped by August's timed call, break the door as he turns on her. POV: August. Beat: terror, clarity, survival.

chapters.title: The Register Restored
chapters.summary: Weeks later, August enters the drowned girl's true name into the restored register and buries Tom beside the archive he guarded. Justice came outside the law, but the record — her record — will outlive everyone. POV: August. Beat: mourning transmuted into quiet, permanent witness.
